floors.title: The Rule
floors.lesson: Prompt instructions are policy, not access control.

floors.title: The Boundary
floors.lesson: Trust boundaries and instruction hierarchy help, but natural-language separation is not process isolation.

floors.title: The Gatekeeper
floors.lesson: Normalization and deterministic input filtering catch known attacks, not the full semantic attack space.

floors.title: The Censor
floors.lesson: Secret-aware output filtering limits the impact of model compromise.

floors.title: The DLP Layer
floors.lesson: Information can be represented in many ways; leakage detection must go beyond literal strings.

floors.title: The Interrogator
floors.lesson: Semantic input classifiers broaden detection, but remain probabilistic controls.

floors.title: The Inspector
floors.lesson: Independent output evaluation catches additional failures, but the evaluator can also misclassify.

floors.title: The Watchtower
floors.lesson: Adaptive attackers exploit repeated attempts; defense must consider conversation-level behavior and attack budgets.

floors.title: The Citadel
floors.lesson: Defense in depth can make prompt injection extremely difficult without turning a secret-bearing LLM into a hard security boundary.
